label: Strictness separator: the box K node holds and the classical GOD_4 root fails on one model
paraphrase: Formal control on a two-point model: one world accessing itself and two candidates, both concrete and existing there, with nothing grounding anything, so both are actual roots; only one of them is GOD_4, and both have the signature's classical-attributes field. In the main model the q.3 a.4 profile puts every candidate in act, lets every candidate cause every candidate in the one respect (CausesIn, a relation distinct from grounding; no bridge between them is assumed) and identifies represented esse and essence; goodness, infinity, eternity, intellect and will are everywhere true, and the six relations potency, more-than, simple priority, component-of, composition and matter/form are empty, so immutability, maximum, firstness, remoteness, simplicity and matter/form exclusion hold vacuously at both candidates. On this model the box K node of the sense fork holds, with the GOD_4 candidate as witness, and the classical GOD_4 root fails. The classical root on this model is equivalent to: some candidate satisfies every other conjunct of the root's body and is the only actual root. The GOD_4 candidate satisfies every other conjunct, and the other candidate is a second actual root that is not GOD_4. A restored-relation control on the same signature and Profile (so the box K node still holds) makes these relations non-empty except component-of: the GOD_4 candidate is more in esse than the other and simply prior to it, causes it and only it, and only the other candidate is in potency, composite and composed of matter and form. There too the classical root fails, it is again equivalent to the rest of its body plus being the only actual root, the GOD_4 candidate satisfies the rest of its body, and maximum and firstness fail at the other candidate. So in both models the classical root fails only because its selected-root uniqueness conjunct (every actual root is the witness, inside PerfectRootAt) has no witness; the box K node asks only that its witness be the one GOD_4 (IsTheOneGod), which does not exclude a second, non-GOD_4 actual root. So the box K node does not entail the classical GOD_4 root. Non-degenerate in this sense: no supplied predicate is emptied so that an attribute fails, the failing conjunct uses ActualRoot, which both nodes contain, and the restored control shows the separation does not rest on the vacuous clauses (only remoteness stays vacuous there). Neither model separates the nodes on any other content (maximum, perfection, firstness, esse/essence identity, matter/form exclusion, remoteness or the case predicates other than IsTheOneGod); that further difference is a syntactic comparison of the two definitions only. A statement about this formal interpretation only; nothing is claimed about the actual world.
